title: Cap. III Resp. Rat. 2: moral means foreknown as apt/possible — not absolutely future before election
pass_a_gloss: Secondly, as to what he urges — that moral means will be of no moment for the very obtaining of the end unless they had been foreseen and accepted by God before the efficacious intention of the end — we confess that such means have their force of causing the end, or of operating toward obtaining the end, from the preceding will of God who ordained and accepted them to such an end: but at the same time we affirm that these means are foreknown and foreseen by God before the end is intended only as apt and conducive to the end, as possible and communicable to all those for whom he wills the end; but they are not foreknown and foreseen as absolutely future in this or that singular man before he is efficaciously elected to glory, that is, destined to the end.
pass_b_english: Second, he presses that moral means would be worthless for obtaining the end unless foreseen and accepted by God before an efficacious intention of the end. We grant such means get their power to cause — or work toward — the end from God's prior will that ordained and accepted them to that end. But we also affirm: before the end is intended, God foreknows those means only as apt and helpful to it, as possible and shareable with all for whom he wills the end — not as absolutely going to happen in this or that particular person before that person is efficaciously elected to glory (destined to the end).
source_text: Secundo, quod urget nullius momenti fore media moralia ad ipsam consecutionem finis, nisi fuissent praevisa & acceptata a Deo ante efficacem intentionem finis, fatemur talia media habere suam vim causandi finem, sive operandi ad consecutionem finis, a praecedente voluntate Dei, qui ea ordinavit & acceptavit ad talem finem: sed simul affirmamus, haec media praecognosci & praevideri a Deo antequam finis intendatur, solummodo tanquam apta & conducentia ad finem, tanquam possibilia & communicabilia illis omnibus quibus vult finem; sed non praesciuntur & praevidentur tanquam absolute futura in hoc aut illo singulari homine, priusquam sit efficaciter ad gloriam electus, id est, ad finem destinatus.
